summary: We have developed a health monitoring software that collects health indicators and enables astronauts to assess their health status and take appropriate action. Communication delays make real-time medical assistance impossible during long-duration space missions. Our solution aims to allow the astronaut to evaluate their health and carry out the first medical actions while awaiting the response of the ground physician
details:
ASTROCARE

Offline Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Long-Duration Space Missions

PROJECT OVERVIEW

AstroCare is a mobile application that enables each astronaut to monitor and assess their own health throughout a long-duration space mission.

Before launch, astronauts create an account and sign in while an Internet connection is available. Once authenticated, the application operates entirely on the device, without requiring a continuous Internet connection.

In its current version, AstroCare tracks four key health indicators: heart rate, body temperature, sleep duration, and mood.

Each newly entered value is analyzed directly on the device using three complementary approaches:

  • Reference thresholds: Each measurement is classified as healthy, requiring attention, or critical.
  • Personal trend analysis: Each measurement is compared against the astronaut's recent health history. This makes it possible to detect unusual changes even when the recorded value remains within the standard reference range.
  • Combined risk assessment: When two health indicators show signs of deterioration, the alert level is increased if the corresponding environmental hazard is present in the current mission environment (spacecraft, space station, rover, lunar base, or Martian base). For example, an abnormal body temperature combined with an abnormal heart rate in an enclosed cabin may indicate a possible infection.

HEALTH MONITORING AND VISUALIZATION FEATURES

AstroCare presents health information through several complementary interfaces:

  • Health Dashboard: A home screen displaying the astronaut's overall health status, with an individual monitoring card for each health indicator.
  • Interactive 3D Human Body Model: A rotatable and zoomable 3D human silhouette in which each body region is color-coded according to its health status. Selecting a body region reveals its reference thresholds, the astronaut's personal measurements, and the corresponding risk information from NASA's Human Research Program.
  • Health Trend Charts: Each health indicator includes interactive graphs covering the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, or the entire mission.
  • Smart Alerts and First Aid Guidance: Alerts include step-by-step first aid instructions tailored to the affected indicator and the direction of the abnormal deviation, as well as warning signs requiring attention.
  • Integrated First Aid Guide: A built-in reference guide that astronauts can access at any time, even without an Internet connection.
  • PDF Health Reports: Health reports are generated directly on the device and can be transmitted to ground-based medical teams through the mission's existing communication channels.

EXPECTED BENEFITS AND IMPACT

During a mission to Mars, communication delays and connectivity interruptions make real-time medical assistance from Earth impossible.

AstroCare provides the crew with an initial level of medical autonomy by enabling astronauts to identify potential health problems early and understand the first steps to take.

The generated health reports provide medical teams on Earth with a clear and structured summary as soon as communication becomes available.

Beyond space exploration, the same offline-first architecture could also benefit remote and isolated environments on Earth, including remote healthcare facilities, polar research stations, and maritime vessels.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

  • Flutter and Dart: Used to develop the mobile application.
  • Local On-Device Storage: Serves as the primary source of truth for health data, ensuring full offline functionality.
  • Supabase: Used for authentication and cloud-based PostgreSQL data backup, with Row-Level Security (RLS) to enforce data access restrictions. It is the application's only online component.
  • GitHub and GitHub Actions: Used for source code management and automated Android application builds.
  • Custom 3D Rendering Engine: Developed entirely by the team in Dart, without relying on external 3D libraries or assets.
  • Custom Charting and PDF Generation Components: Developed by the team in Dart, without external charting or PDF libraries.
  • AI-Assisted Development: AI assistants, including Claude and Arena, supported the code-writing process. All generated code was reviewed and validated by the development team.

INNOVATION AND CREATIVITY

AstroCare introduces several innovative approaches to astronaut health monitoring:

  • Fully Self-Contained 3D Visualization: The 3D human body model is generated and rendered directly by the application, without requiring external 3D files, assets, or network access.
  • Beyond Fixed Thresholds: Health analysis combines standard reference thresholds with each astronaut's personal health baseline, enabling the detection of individual health deviations.
  • Context-Aware Risk Assessment: Health indicators are analyzed together in relation to the five major hazards of human spaceflight identified by NASA, taking the current mission environment into account.
  • Communication-Independent Reporting: Health reports are generated locally as standard PDF documents, making them compatible with existing mission communication systems.

DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS AND CONSTRAINTS

AstroCare was designed around the specific challenges of long-duration space missions.

1. Space-to-Earth Communication Latency

Most application features operate entirely offline. Initial authentication takes place before the mission, while health data is stored and analyzed locally. Internet connectivity is not required for routine health monitoring.

2. Stress and Fatigue

The application minimizes cognitive load through a limited set of health indicators, a straightforward dashboard, and clear, easy-to-understand instructions.

3. Accessibility and Usability

Health statuses are never communicated through color alone. Each status is accompanied by an icon and a descriptive label, with a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1. The application supports both English and French.

4. Data Privacy and Security

Each astronaut is restricted to reading and writing their own health records through individual access controls and database-level Row-Level Security policies.

5. Visual Identity

The application follows the official NASA Space Apps Challenge color palette and typography guidelines to maintain a consistent visual identity.

6. Current Limitations

AstroCare is a research prototype and is not a certified medical device.

  • Health measurements are currently entered manually rather than collected through connected medical sensors.
  • Reference thresholds are indicative values based on healthy adults on Earth and have not been validated for the specific physiological conditions of spaceflight.
  • The first aid instructions provide general guidance and have not been medically validated.
  • The application is intended to support health awareness and preliminary risk identification, not replace professional medical diagnosis or treatment.

7. HOW TO DOWNLOAD, INSTALL, AND TEST ASTROCARE

To test AstroCare on an Android device, follow the instructions below:

Step 1 – Access the GitHub Repository

Open the GitHub repository using the link provided in the Project section above.

Step 2 – Access GitHub Actions

Click on the Actions tab to view the project's automated build workflows.

Step 3 – Download the Latest Application Build

  • Select the most recent workflow run.
  • Open the latest successful workflow execution.
  • Scroll down to the Artifacts section at the bottom of the page.
  • Click on the artifact named astrocare-apk-v2-5-16 to start downloading the application package.

Step 4 – Install the Application

Once the download is complete:

  • Extract the downloaded ZIP archive.
  • Locate the APK file.
  • Transfer it to your Android device if necessary.
  • Enable installation from unknown sources in your Android device settings, if prompted.
  • Install the APK and launch AstroCare.

Step 5 – Create an Account or Use the Test Credentials

Once the application is launched, you can create your own account or use the following test account to access the application immediately:

Test Account Credentials:

  • Email: stevelove2040@gmail.com
  • Password: galilee

You can now explore AstroCare's features and test its offline health monitoring capabilities.

Important: The test account is provided for evaluation purposes. Internet access is required for initial authentication, but the application's core health monitoring features are designed to work offline after login.
